summary: Full Riftbound test pass: headless tracer invariants + monkey gameplay-flow + per-card playtest on N untested cards. Returns one merged report.
logs: auto-fixing 41 confirmed bugs across 13 files (same-file serialized)

findings.what: After playing Unlicensed Armory, the engine offers `activateAbility` on it even though player-1 controls zero units (base holds only the gear itself; both battlefield zones are empty).
findings.why_wrong: Unlicensed Armory's activated ability reads "Discard 1, [Exhaust]: Choose a friendly unit. …". Rule 355.10.c uses this exact wording as its example of a TARGET ("'Choose a friendly unit. The next time it would die this turn…' targets a friendly unit"). Rule 355.8 states "In order to put a spell or ability on the chain, valid choices must be made for all targets." With no friendly unit on the board, the ability has no legal target and cannot be put on the chain, so it must not appear in the legal-moves list. Offering it risks the player paying the discard+exhaust cost for an ability that can never finalize.
findings.reason: Trace step 17 shows player-1 base=[Unlicensed Armory only], both battlefields empty, yet moves[] includes activateAbility on player-1-main-38-ogn-023-298. The activateAbility condition (chain-moves.ts:606-771) and enumerator (chain-moves.ts:772-961) validate zone/owner/timing/cost (energy, power, xp, exhaust, kill) but never resolve the ability effect's target descriptor — condition falls through to `return true` at :770 and enumerator pushes at :956 with no effect-target check. Unlicensed Armory's effect has target {controller:"friendly", type:"unit"} (unlicensed-armory.ts:43), which per 355.10.c is a target and per 355.8 requires a valid choice to put the ability on the chain.

findings.why_wrong: The ability text 'Choose a friendly unit. The next time it would die this turn…' targets a friendly unit — rule 355.10.c cites this exact wording as a targeted effect. Rule 355.8 requires valid choices for all targets before an ability can go on the chain. With no friendly units on the board, activateAbility should not have been a legal move in step 21's moves[], and the chain item in step 22 should never have been created.
findings.reason: activateAbility's condition (chain-moves.ts:606-770) and enumerator (772-960) check zone/owner/timing/cost (energy, power, xp, exhaust, kill) but never gate on the ability effect's target — condition returns true at :770 unconditionally after cost checks. The reducer (:962-1024) pays cost then addToChain at :1019-1023 with no target-selection pendingChoice. Contrast cards.ts:413-438 spellEffectHasLegalTargets which implements 355.8 for spells but is never called from activateAbility. Trace step 21 moves[] offers activateAbility on ogn-023-298 while base=[gear only] and both bfZones=[]; step 22 shows Armory exhausted, pendingChoice=null, and passChainPriority available (chain active). Unlicensed Armory's effect (unlicensed-armory.ts:43) declares target:{controller:"friendly",type:"unit"}, which per rule 355.10.c is a caster-chosen target and per 355.8 must have ≥1 valid choice to go on the chain.

findings.what: The 'Discard 1' portion of the activation cost was not paid: hand is identical before/after (5 player-1 cards, same IDs), trash stayed at 0, and no pendingChoice was raised to pick which card to discard. Only the [Exhaust] half of the cost was applied (exhausted false→true).
findings.why_wrong: The card definition correctly declares cost:{discard:1, exhaust:true}. Rule 357.2 requires all non-standard cost components to be paid; rule 422.1/422.3 defines discard-as-cost as moving a card from hand to trash and requires it be completable. The engine processed exhaust but silently skipped the discard component — the player got the ability for free (minus tap).
findings.reason: Card def declares cost:{discard:1, exhaust:true} (unlicensed-armory.ts:17). The activateAbility reducer's cost-paying block (chain-moves.ts:976-1003) calls deductAbilityCost (energy/power only, lines 435-491), then handles cost.exhaust (982-984), cost.xp (987-990), cost.kill (994-1002) — there is no branch for cost.discard, and no pendingChoice is raised to pick the card. The condition block (685-768) likewise never checks cost.discard. Trace step 21→22 confirms: identical 5 player-1 handIds, trash 0→0, pendingChoiceVisible=false, exhausted false→true, ability placed on chain — discard component of the cost was silently skipped, violating rules 357.2/422.3.

findings.what: The 'Discard 1' component of Unlicensed Armory's activation cost was not collected. Across steps 21→22→23: dom.handCount stays 5, handIds are byte-identical, trash stays 0. Only the [Exhaust] half of the cost was applied (exhausted false→true).
findings.why_wrong: Rule 204.1.b: on activated abilities the Base Cost is everything before the ':' — here 'Discard 1, [Exhaust]'. Rule 377.3.b.1 routes activation through the same finalize/pay-cost steps as playing a card; the discard is mandatory and non-optional. The card def declares cost:{discard:1, exhaust:true} but the engine only honored exhaust.
findings.reason: The activateAbility reducer's pay-cost block (chain-moves.ts:976-1003) handles cost.exhaust (:982), cost.xp (:987-990), cost.kill (:994-1002), and delegates energy/power to deductAbilityCost (:978 → defined :435-491, which reads only cost.energy and cost.power). The word "discard" does not appear anywhere in chain-moves.ts. The card def declares cost:{discard:1, exhaust:true} at /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/ogn/unlicensed-armory.ts:17. Trace steps 21→22→23 confirm: exhausted flips false→true on player-1-main-38-ogn-023-298, but handIds are byte-identical, dom.handCount stays 5, trash stays 0, and no pendingChoice for discard selection was raised (pendingChoiceVisible:false). Rule 204.1.b: Base Cost is everything before ':' — the Discard 1 is a mandatory part of the activation cost that the engine silently drops.

findings.what: Gold gear token enters ready instead of exhausted

findings.reason: parseCreateTokenEffect gear branch (index.ts:1964-1985) captures `(exhausted)?` as gearMatch[4] but never reads it — the returned effect is `{type:'create-token', token:{name:'Gold',type:'gear'}}` with no exhausted flag. Downstream, effect-executor.ts:896-898 only sets exhausted:true for non-gear tokens (`if (tokenDef.type !== "gear")`) and has no path to read an exhausted field from the effect, so Gold gear tokens enter ready. bushwhack.ts (sfd-004-221) has no hand-authored abilities and relies on this parser; sfd-074-221 (Pickpocket) likewise says "play a Gold gear token exhausted". findings.what: /tutor endpoint under-grants domain power for cards with >2 pips of the same domain
findings.expected: Tutoring Time Warp (powerCost = 4×mind) should grant ≥4 mind power so it is immediately playable
findings.observed: Only {mind:2} granted (server.ts:2268 Object.fromEntries((powerCost).map(d=>[d,2])) collapses duplicates); playSpell CONDITION_FAILED until manual addResources
findings.reason: Time Warp's powerCost is derived as ["mind","mind","mind","mind"] (all-cards.ts:852-862 derivePowerCost from ogn.json power:4, domains:["mind"]). server.ts:2268 does Object.fromEntries((def.powerCost).map(d=>[d,2])), which collapses the four duplicate "mind" keys to {mind:2}. canAffordCard (card-lookup.ts:240-249) sums pips to needed={mind:4} and fails since 2<4, so playSpell returns CONDITION_FAILED until manual addResources.

findings.what: Extra-turn effect not parsed from rules text
findings.expected: Rules text 'Take a turn after this one.' should parse to an extra-turn effect on the spell ability
findings.observed: parseExtraTurnEffect regex (parser/index.ts:1935) requires the word 'extra' — /^Take an extra turn after this one\.?$/i — so it does not match; the spell's chain effect contained only {type:'banish',target:'self'} with no extra-turn component
findings.reason: Card ogn-122-298 rulesText is "Take a turn after this one. Banish this." (time-warp.ts:12). parseExtraTurnEffect at parser/index.ts:1935 uses /^Take an extra turn after this one\.?$/i, which requires the literal word "extra" and so fails to match "Take a turn after this one." The alternate static-parser.ts:1086 has the same "extra" requirement. No other parser branch handles this phrasing, so the extra-turn effect is dropped and only the banish-self clause survives.

findings.what: 'Take a turn after this one' had no gameplay effect
findings.expected: After resolving Time Warp and ending the turn, player-1 should take the next turn (turn 2) before player-2
findings.observed: endTurn advanced to turn 3 with player-1 active and players.turnsTaken = {p1:2, p2:1} — normal alternation; player-2 took turn 2. Engine has no 'extra-turn' case in effect-executor.ts
findings.reason: Time Warp (ogn-122-298) has no gameplay effect wired. Card def at /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/ogn/time-warp.ts:4-15 carries only rulesText, no abilities/effects field. The effect-executor switch at effect-executor.ts:319-1352 has no extra-turn/additional-turn case (unknown types hit default:break at :1349). The rule-734 primitives in operations/turn-queue.ts:29 (enqueueExtraTurn) and :75 (nextTurnPlayer) have zero non-test callers — grep for enqueueExtraTurn|pendingExtraTurns|nextTurnPlayer across engine+cards returns nothing outside turn-queue.ts itself, and its own docstring (:16-19) notes the flow layer "will consult" it "once it lands". riftbound-flow.ts turn.onBegin (:147) reads context.getCurrentPlayer() from the core flow manager without consulting pendingExtraTurns, and moves/turn.ts:48 endTurn just calls flow.endPhase(). So resolving Time Warp mutates no state and endTurn advances by normal seat-order rotation — matching the observed {p1:2, p2:1} turnsTaken.

findings.what: 'Banish this' left the card in trash, not banishment
findings.expected: After Time Warp resolves, the card should be in the banishment zone
findings.observed: zones.trash contained player-1-main-999-ogn-122-298; zones.banishment was empty. playSpell reducer (cards.ts:1158) moves the spell to trash at play time; the chain's {type:'banish',target:'self'} did not relocate it to banishment on resolution
findings.reason: Verified at runtime that getCardRegistry() gives ogn-122-298 the spell effect {type:"banish", target:"self"} (bare string). playSpell reducer moves the spell to trash at cards.ts:1158 and puts that effect on the chain. On resolution, executeResolvedItem's choose-target guard at chain-moves.ts:198-228 reads effect.target as a TargetDescriptor and tests target.type !== "self"; for the bare string "self", target.type is undefined so the guard is entered, resolveTarget is called with {..."self", quantity:"all"} (→ {0:"s",1:"e",2:"l",3:"f",quantity:"all"}), which target-resolver.ts:88-156 treats as a generic board query and explicitly excludes sourceCardId (line 150-151). boundTargets is thus set to board cards (or [] / pendingChoice), so getTargetIds in the banish handler (effect-executor.ts:826) never returns the spell's own instance id. The card remains in trash and banishment stays empty — matches the observed state.

findings.what: Static 'Your tokens enter ready' is not applied when tokens are created
findings.expected: With Renata Glasc on board, a friendly Recruit unit token created via create-token should enter with exhausted=false
findings.observed: Token token-recruit-…-0 entered base with exhausted=true. effect-executor.ts:895-898 unconditionally sets exhausted=true for non-gear tokens and never consults Renata's static grant-keyword(EntersReady) ability
findings.reason: create-token handler at effect-executor.ts:895-898 unconditionally sets exhausted=true for non-gear tokens (`if (tokenDef.type !== "gear") { ctx.counters.setFlag(tokenId, "exhausted", true); }`) without consulting any enters-ready source. Renata Glasc (sfd-171-221) is defined as a static grant-keyword(EntersReady) ability targeting friendly token units; the static-abilities grant-keyword handler (static-abilities.ts:357-387) only appends the keyword to grantedKeywords meta and never clears the exhausted flag. Unlike the play-card path (cards.ts:732-736), the create-token path checks neither hasStaticEffect(…,"enter-ready"), nor consumeEntersReadyReplacement, nor granted EntersReady keywords, so Recruit tokens enter exhausted even with Renata on board.

findings.what: Created token surfaced with raw instance id as name and type 'unknown' in the state snapshot
findings.expected: Token should display as name='Recruit', type='unit', might=1 (values registered at effect-executor.ts:904)
findings.observed: pw state showed {id:'token-recruit-1785955197888-0', name:'token-recruit-1785955197888-0', type:'unknown', exhausted:true}; UI rendered a generic cardback with no name/might
findings.reason: buildGameSnapshot resolves card defs via the module-level `registry` = getCardRegistry() from @tcg/riftbound-cards (server.ts:114), a static Map built only from set JSON. Token definitions are registered only in the engine's getGlobalCardRegistry() (token.ts:133 under `token-def-<slug>`; effect-executor.ts:904 under the instance id). At server.ts:663 `registry.get(cardInstance.definitionId)` — definitionId is `token-def-recruit` per chain-moves.ts:106 — returns undefined, so the fallbacks fire: cardType 'unknown' (server.ts:673), name=cardId i.e. the raw instance id (server.ts:681), might undefined (server.ts:680). Matches the observed snapshot exactly.

findings.what: Triggered ability "When you play a card on an opponent's turn" can never fire — the engine's restriction check for the parser-emitted `on-opponent-turn` type is a hardcoded `return false` stub
findings.expected: Playing a card during an opponent's turn while Viktor is in play creates a 1-Might Recruit unit token at your base
findings.observed: trigger-matcher.ts restrictionSatisfied() case 'on-opponent-turn' returns false unconditionally (TODO stub), so the trigger is always blocked. Could not exercise in goldfish (opponent turn auto-resolves with no reaction window), but code path guarantees no token would ever spawn.
findings.reason: restrictionSatisfied() case "on-opponent-turn" at trigger-matcher.ts:129-131 is `// TODO(on-opponent-turn): active-player check not exposed here.` followed by `return false;` — an unconditional stub. It is invoked from triggerMatchesEvent() at :261-266, which returns false when any restriction fails, so any trigger carrying this restriction never matches. The parser emits exactly this restriction for Viktor's text at riftbound-cards/src/parser/index.ts:3982-3988 (`pattern: /^When you play a card on an opponent's turn,\s*/i`, `restrictions: [{ type: "on-opponent-turn" }]`). ven-176-166 reaches this path: ven.json ships `abilities: []`, but adaptJsonCard() (all-cards.ts:805-807) maps an empty/null-only array to `abilities: undefined`, so enrichCard() (enrich-cards.ts:22-38) re-parses rulesText at load time and attaches the parser-emitted `on-opponent-turn` restriction. The engine stub therefore guarantees the Recruit token never spawns.

findings.what: "You may play me to an open battlefield" is not honored — only location:'base' is offered as a playUnit destination
findings.expected: playUnit moves with location = each open (empty) battlefield in addition to base
findings.observed: Both battlefields were empty but availableMoves listed only {moveId:'playUnit', params:{location:'base'}}. The static ability is emitted as {type:'play-restriction', allowedLocation:'an open battlefield'} which the engine has no handler for (grep for allowedLocation/play-restriction in riftbound-engine returns nothing).
findings.reason: playUnit.enumerate (cards.ts:607-670) only ever pushes location:'base' (lines 619, 639, 662); playUnit.condition (cards.ts:517-522) rejects any battlefield location unless the card has the Ambush keyword. Sai Scout (ogn-174-298) has no Ambush. Its "You may play me to an open battlefield" text is parsed by static-parser.ts:514-528 into {type:'play-restriction', allowedLocation:'an open battlefield'} (present in ogn.json:6344-6345), but grep for 'play-restriction'/'allowedLocation' in riftbound-engine/src/ returns zero hits — the engine has no consumer of this ability, so open battlefields are never offered as playUnit destinations.

findings.what: [Vision] trigger softlocks the game — pendingChoice cannot be resolved
findings.expected: After the Vision trigger resolves, a resolvePendingChoice move is enumerated so the player can act on the revealed top card and play continues
findings.observed: The 'look' effect sets pendingChoice with fields {playerId, options, ...} but resolvePendingChoice's condition/enumerator gate on choice.prompter (undefined) and iterate choice.revealed (undefined). Server /moves returns only [concede]; endTurn and every other move are blocked by the pendingChoice, leaving the game stuck.
findings.reason: The `case "look"` handler (effect-executor.ts:1093-1101) — which Vision triggers via the parser (effect-keyword-parser.ts:506-512, parser/index.ts:5236) — sets pendingChoice as `{type:"reveal-and-pick", playerId, options, onPicked, onRest, remaining, sourceCardId}` using an `as RiftboundGameState["pendingChoice"]` cast that bypasses the real `RevealAndPickChoice` shape (game-state.ts:302-329: `prompter`, `revealer`, `revealed`, `filter?`, `onPicked`). resolvePendingChoice's condition then fails at pending-choice.ts:100 (`choice.prompter !== context.params.playerId` → undefined !== id → return false) and the enumerator returns [] at pending-choice.ts:134 (same guard; and line 144 would iterate undefined `choice.revealed`). Every other move short-circuits on `state.pendingChoice` (e.g. turn.ts:33, resources.ts:31, cards.ts:493), so after Sai Scout's Vision trigger fires the only enumerated move is concede — a softlock.

findings.what: [Vision] semantics wrong — pendingChoice is configured to draw the card if picked and recycle it if not, with no option to leave it on top
findings.expected: Per rulesText "look at the top card … you may recycle it": choose either recycle-to-bottom or leave-on-top; never draw
findings.observed: pendingChoice = {type:'reveal-and-pick', onPicked:'draw', onRest:'recycle', remaining:1}. Picking would move the card to hand (onPickedTargetZone('draw')); declining would recycle it — the mandatory-recycle-or-draw pair does not match Vision.
findings.reason: Sai Scout (ogn-174-298) parses [Vision] into a play-self trigger with effect `{type:"look", amount:1, from:"deck", then:{recycle:1}}` (parser/parsers/effect-keyword-parser.ts:506-513; verified by parser/__tests__/keywords/vision.test.ts:57-64). When executed, the `case "look"` handler at effect-executor.ts:1080-1102 ignores `then` and builds pendingChoice with `onPicked: effect.onPicked ?? "draw"` (line 1094) and `onRest: effect.onRest ?? "recycle"` (line 1095) — the parsed effect carries neither field, so the defaults apply. The comment at :1084-1085 even names Vision as using this draw/recycle default. This is the wrong semantics for Vision: per rulesText the choice is recycle-to-bottom or leave-on-top; there is no draw outcome and declining must leave the card on top, not recycle it. (The reducer/type layer at game-definition/moves/pending-choice.ts:65-77 and types/game-state.ts:328 don't even recognize `"draw"` or `onRest`, so the resulting state is additionally malformed — but the configured intent is still draw-if-picked/recycle-if-not, matching the finding.)

findings.what: "When I hold" trigger fired while the unit was at base, not at a battlefield
findings.expected: Per rule 383.4.d / 383.4.d.2.a, a unit's "When I hold" ability triggers only when that unit is present at a battlefield the controller holds during the Beginning phase
findings.observed: Unit was in zone `base`, battlefield-player-1-bf-unl-205-219 was empty, player-1 held it and scored — Enthusiastic Promoter's hold trigger was still put on the chain (chain item {cardId: player-1-main-999-unl-043-219, effect:{type:'buff', target:{type:'unit',quantity:'all'}}})
findings.reason: trigger-matcher.ts:164-178 — for `on:"self"` on a `hold` event ({playerId, battlefieldId}, no cardId), line 169 only checks battlefieldId when `card.zone === "battlefieldRow"` (battlefield cards). A unit at `base` skips that branch and hits line 175, which only rejects when `event.playerId !== card.owner`. Since player-1 owns the unit and player-1 held, the check passes and the trigger matches. Rule 383.4.d.2.a requires the unit to be present AT the held battlefield; the matcher never checks `card.zone === "battlefield-" + event.battlefieldId` for unit self-hold triggers. Card ability comes from parser/index.ts:3676 (`{event:"hold", on:"self"}`), zone `base` passes the scan filter at trigger-matcher.ts:291, and the hold event is emitted at riftbound-flow.ts:306.

findings.what: Hold-trigger buff effect did not apply +1 Might to units, and lacks the 'here' location scope
findings.expected: rulesText: "[Buff] all units here" — every unit at the same location as Enthusiastic Promoter gets a +1 Might buff (if it doesn't already have one)
findings.observed: Chain effect target was {type:'unit', quantity:'all'} with no location filter (should be scoped to 'here'). After passChainPriority resolved the trigger, both co-located units still had might=2 and meta.buffed=false; only Legion Rearguard got __flags.buffed=true while Enthusiastic Promoter itself did not — no visible +1 Might on either. unl.json ability has effects:[] (empty sequence).
findings.reason: Runtime registry for unl-043-219 (built from enthusiastic-promoter.ts via enrichCards→parseAbilities, not unl.json) yields effect {type:"buff", target:{type:"unit", quantity:"all"}} — no location:"here". Root cause: the buff regex alternation `(?:unit|units)` matches "unit" first, so for "Buff all units here" match[1]="all unit" and the trailing "s here" is dropped, so line 361's `.includes("here")` never fires. Separately, the executor's buff branch calls ctx.counters.setFlag(id,"buffed",true) which writes meta.__flags.buffed (core operations-impl.ts:532), while every Might reader checks top-level meta.buffed (effect-executor.ts:149, static-abilities.ts:123, cards.ts:216), so no +1 Might is ever observed — matching the report's meta.buffed=false / __flags.buffed=true observation.

findings.what: No target-selection prompt for "Choose two units"
findings.expected: Playing the spell should prompt the player to choose two unit targets (pendingChoice or per-target playSpell moves) before it goes on the chain
findings.observed: playSpell move had no target params and no pendingChoice appeared; the spell went straight onto the chain with an untargeted fight effect, then resolved after passChainPriority with no player input
findings.reason: clash-of-giants.ts:4-15 defines the SpellCard with no `abilities` field at all. The server registers cards from the TS defs (server.ts:983→987 via makeLookupPayload at server.ts:738, which passes `def.abilities` — undefined here), so getAbilities() at card-lookup.ts:164-166 returns []. In playSpell (moves/cards.ts): the enumerator (lines ~1043-1095) finds no spell ability, so `spellEffect?.target` is undefined and it emits `{cardId, playerId}` with no `targets`; the reducer (lines ~1111-1145) reads `spellAbility?.effect` as undefined and calls addToChain with `effect: undefined, targets: undefined`, never setting a pendingChoice. Thus the spell goes on the chain with no target-selection step and resolves after passChainPriority with no player input — exactly the observed behavior. (Minor: the chain item's effect is actually undefined, not a fight effect, since the card has no ability implementation.)

findings.what: Target restriction wrong: hardcoded one friendly + one enemy instead of any two units
findings.expected: rulesText "Choose two units" imposes no controller restriction — any two units (both friendly, both enemy, or mixed) should be legal targets
findings.observed: Chain effect was {type:'fight', attacker:{controller:'friendly',type:'unit'}, defender:{controller:'enemy',type:'unit'}} — parser (parseFightEffect in effect-parser.ts:417) hardcodes friendly-vs-enemy
findings.reason: Card unl-110-219 (clash-of-giants.ts:4-15) has rulesText "Choose two units. They deal damage equal to their Mights to each other." and no explicit `abilities` field, so enrich-cards.ts:20-38 runs parseAbilities on it. Executed getCardRegistry().get("unl-110-219") via bun and the runtime abilities are exactly [{type:"spell",effect:{type:"fight",attacker:{controller:"friendly",type:"unit"},defender:{controller:"enemy",type:"unit"}}}]. The hardcoding lives in parseFightEffect at parser/index.ts:1800-1809 (attacker:{controller:"friendly"}, defender:{controller:"enemy"}) and duplicated at parser/parsers/effect-parser.ts:425-426 (the location cited in the finding). target-resolver.ts:113-123 filters candidates by these controller values (friendly → owner===playerId only; enemy → owner!==playerId only), and effect-executor.ts:1030-1064 passes the descriptors through resolveTarget, so the spell cannot legally pick two friendly or two enemy units despite the rules text imposing no controller restriction.

findings.what: Spell resolved with zero effect instead of two units damaging each other
findings.expected: With two 2-Might Legion Rearguards on board and "Choose two units", each should deal 2 damage to the other (both die → trash)
findings.observed: After resolution both units remained at base with might=2, damage=0, meta unchanged; trash=1 (only the spell). Game log shows only 'dev cast Clash of Giants' + priority passes, no damage/kill entries. The fight executor found no enemy unit (defenders[0] undefined) and silently no-op'd.
findings.reason: parseFightEffect (index.ts:1800-1808) hardcodes attacker={controller:"friendly"} and defender={controller:"enemy"} for any text ending in "deal damage equal to their Mights to each other", ignoring the actual target clause. Verified by running the parser on Clash of Giants' rulesText — it emits {type:"spell", effect:{type:"fight", attacker:{controller:"friendly",type:"unit"}, defender:{controller:"enemy",type:"unit"}}} instead of two controller-agnostic unit targets. The fight effect carries no .target field, so cards.ts:1067-1092 enumerates no play-time targets and chain-moves.ts:197-229 sets no pendingChoice; execution goes straight to effect-executor.ts:1030-1063, where resolveTarget on {controller:"enemy",type:"unit"} returns [] (both Legion Rearguards are the caster's own), defenders[0] is undefined, and the guard at :1051 silently no-ops — matching the observed zero-effect resolution with only the spell in trash.

findings.what: playSpell not offered when zero friendly units are in play
findings.expected: Overt Operation is an [Action] with no target requirement ('for each friendly unit' and 'buff all friendly units' both accept zero); should be castable on an empty board
findings.observed: With 9 energy / 2 body power and no units on board, playSpell for player-1-main-999-ogn-153-298 was absent from moves; it appeared only after a unit was played to base
findings.reason: spellEffectHasLegalTargets (cards.ts:413-438) has no branch for effect.type === "for-each", so it falls through to the generic target check at lines 430-434. Overt Operation's for-each sub-effect (overt-operation.ts:28-30) carries target: {controller:"friendly", type:"unit"} with no quantity field; targetDescriptorIsSatisfiable (cards.ts:459-476) sees qty=undefined, computes zeroTargetsLegal=false, and calls resolveTarget which returns [] on an empty board, so it returns false. The sequence .every() at line 426 then fails, and the enumerator at line 1059 skips the card. Per rule 355.10.d "for each friendly unit" is a programmatic selection, not a caster-chosen target, so 355.8 should not gate it — zero units must be legal.

findings.what: 'Then buff all friendly units' does not surface the buff in game state or UI
findings.expected: After resolution, Legion Rearguard should have meta.buffed=true and the UI should render a +1 might buff indicator (effective might 3)
findings.observed: Server state shows meta.buffed=false while a leaked meta.__flags.buffed=true is present on the same card; UI DOM has no buff class/badge and might displays as 2. Game log records only 'dev cast Overt Operation' with no buff line.
findings.reason: The "buff" effect handler at effect-executor.ts:452 writes via ctx.counters.setFlag(targetId, "buffed", true), which core operations-impl.ts:526-532 stores at cardMetas[id].__flags.buffed — not at top-level meta.buffed. Every reader checks top-level meta.buffed instead: effect-executor.ts:448 (already-buffed guard), target-resolver.ts:274 (effective might), static-abilities.ts:123/132, and the server serializer at server.ts:670-679, which special-cases only __flags.exhausted and spreads the stale baseMeta (initialized buffed:false at server.ts:724). Result: serialized meta.buffed=false with leaked __flags.buffed=true; renderer.js:622 (card.meta?.buffed) renders no badge and might stays at base 2. Matches the observed state exactly.

findings.observed: executeMove(playUnit) resolved immediately at full cost (energy 34→22, order 4→1 = 10E+3order paid); no pendingChoice, no chain item, Rearguard remained alive on base

Even forcing playUnit with paidAdditionalCost:true does nothing: the reducer re-derives the optional cost via getOptionalPlayCost() which returns undefined for this card, so paidAdditionalCostActual stays false and the play-self event is emitted with paidAdditionalCost:false — the trigger's {type:'paid-additional-cost'} condition never passes.
findings.reason: Runtime-verified: getCardRegistry().get("sfd-109-221").abilities contains (a) {type:"static", effect:{type:"additional-cost-option", additionalCost:":rb_rune_body::rb_rune_body:"}} and (b) a play-self trigger with condition:{type:"paid-additional-cost"}. getOptionalPlayCost() at cards.ts:113-129 only returns for keyword=Accelerate or for static/additional-cost-option with ability.cost.kill; it reads ability.cost (undefined here — data lives in ability.effect.additionalCost) and has no branch for a pure power-pip additional cost, so it returns undefined. findings.what: End-of-turn triggered ability does nothing

findings.expected: Per the ruling: when Thrill of the Hunt resolves, the banished unit is added to the chain as a pending item [354.2], the spell finishes, Abandoned Hall's play-spell trigger becomes pending after the unit [419.4.a/383.2.c], the unit finalizes/resolves onto Abandoned Hall first [337.1.b/337.2], and then the trigger's target is chosen — with the replayed unit present at Abandoned Hall as a valid choice for the +1 Might.

findings.expected: When finalizing Alpha Strike on the chain, the caster first chooses a friendly unit as an explicit standard target, then chooses up to N enemy units at battlefields as split targets, where N = that friendly unit's current might. The caster may choose fewer than N (including zero). All target choices are locked at finalization (355.14.a-c, 355.15).
findings.observed: Board: p1 main phase; friendly Darius (5 might) at base; 3 enemy units at a battlefield (one damaged); 28 energy + every power domain available; Alpha Strike in hand. Engine offers ZERO legal playSpell moves for Alpha Strike, and direct playSpell attempts (no targets / friendly-unit target / subset of enemy units) all return CONDITION_FAILED. No friendly-unit choice or enemy split-target choice is ever surfaced. Code confirms: (1) resolveAmount() only handles might:"self" — the card's might:{controller:"friendly",type:"unit"} falls through to 0, so no friendly-unit selection exists; (2) the enemy target descriptor is quantity:"all" and the damage handler ignores split:true entirely, so there is no caster-chosen up-to-N enemy subset; (3) no pendingChoice is raised, so nothing is locked at finalization.
findings.notes: Structural divergence, not a setup gap. The targeting flow the ruling describes (explicit friendly-unit target → might-bounded split-target selection → lock at finalization) is unimplemented. alpha-strike.ts already carries a FIXME acknowledging the kill-count approximation; the split/might targeting is similarly stubbed. Relevant code: packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effect-executor.ts:183-188 (might amount), :375-427 (damage handler ignores split); packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/alpha-strike.ts (quantity:"all" target, no friendly-unit target). Screenshot: /tmp/ruling-6b3effc73787ce91.png

findings.expected: Per rules 355.14.e/f/g and 359.3.f.2: when Alpha Strike resolves, the caster chooses how to distribute damage equal to the friendly unit's current might among the chosen enemy units; each chosen target must receive at least 1 damage; all available damage must be distributed; the distribution is a resolution-time choice (not fixed at finalization).
findings.observed: Alpha Strike cannot be played at all — playSpell returns CONDITION_FAILED even with a friendly might-5 unit and 3 enemy units on battlefields. Root cause: spellEffectHasLegalTargets (cards.ts:413-438) recurses into the sequence and treats the for-each sub-effect's `{filter:"damaged"}` target descriptor as a caster-chosen target that must resolve non-empty; the resolver ctx passed at cards.ts:978 lacks getCardMeta so the `damaged` filter (target-resolver.ts:222-223) always returns false, so the play condition can never be satisfied. Separately, split damage is not implemented: the damage effect handler (effect-executor.ts:375-427) ignores `split: true` and applies the full `amount` to every target; there is no pendingChoice/distribution prompt, no min-1-per-target enforcement, and zero references to `split` anywhere in the engine's ability execution code. If the play-condition bug were fixed, the engine would deal the friendly unit's full might to each enemy unit rather than splitting it.
findings.notes: Setup: fresh goldfish game, tutored unl-192-219 (Alpha Strike) + unl-105-219 (Imposing Challenger, might 5); duplicateCard placed 1 friendly copy at battlefield-player-1 and 3 enemy copies at battlefield-player-2. playSpell rejected with CONDITION_FAILED both before and after adding 1 damage to an enemy unit. Code refs: /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effect-executor.ts:375-427 (no split handling), /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/cards.ts:413-476 & 975-992 (over-strict target-legality gate on for-each), /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-types/src/abilities/effect-types.ts:161 (split field defined but unused). Screenshot: /tmp/ruling-da6fb2fa426580ff.png

findings.expected: Per ruling: Alpha Strike chooses a friendly unit as a target at play time. If that unit remains a friendly unit on the board when Alpha Strike resolves (even if it moved locations), it deals damage equal to its Might split among enemy units at battlefields. If the unit left the board / stopped being a unit / stopped being friendly, it is an illegal target under 359.3.e.2, its Might referent returns null under 359.3.e.12, and Alpha Strike deals no damage.
findings.observed: The engine's Alpha Strike implementation never chooses a friendly unit as a target. The card def (packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/alpha-strike.ts) encodes the friendly unit only as an amount expression `amount:{might:{controller:"friendly",type:"unit"}}`. playSpell (cards.ts:1063-1092) only enumerates play-time targets for the top-level effect.target — Alpha Strike's top level is a `sequence`, so no target is bound to the chain item. resolveAmount (effect-executor.ts:167-224) handles only `might:"self"`; for the object form it falls through and returns 0, so the damage amount is always 0 regardless of whether a friendly unit is on the board. executeResolvedItem (chain-moves.ts:155-234) performs no target-legality re-check on stored chain targets, so rule 359.3.e.2/5/12 is not modeled at all. Additionally, spellEffectHasLegalTargets (cards.ts:413-477) requires the sequence's for-each sub-effect target ({controller:"enemy",filter:"damaged"}) to resolve non-empty, so playSpell for Alpha Strike is rejected (CONDITION_FAILED) unless a damaged enemy unit already exists — confirmed empirically during a showdown with an undamaged enemy Wizened Elder at a battlefield and a friendly Legion Rearguard at base.
findings.notes: Net effect vs. the ruling: (a) 'friendly unit still on board → deals its Might in damage' — engine deals 0 (DIVERGES). (b) 'friendly unit becomes illegal → deals no damage' — engine deals 0 too, but coincidentally: there is no chosen target to become illegal and no null-referent handling; the amount resolver simply doesn't support this shape. The 359.3.e illegal-target / null-referent pathway is not implemented, and no implemented Reaction spell with a functional return-to-hand/kill-friendly effect exists to remove the unit while on the chain (Retreat/Gust/Deathgrip/Heedless Resurrection/Star-Crossed are all data-only stubs with no `abilities` array). Screenshot: /tmp/ruling-97a79a0eeb51f1ea.png. Key files: packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/alpha-strike.ts; packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effect-executor.ts:167-224,375-420; packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/cards.ts:413-477,906-994,1063-1162; packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/chain-moves.ts:155-234.

findings.expected: Per the ruling and rules 355.14.h/.h.1: after finalizing Alpha Strike with a friendly 3-might unit and 3 enemy unit targets, if the friendly unit's might is reduced to 2 before resolution (e.g. via Stupefy), the engine should prompt the controller to drop exactly 1 target (no more), then distribute 2 damage across the 2 remaining targets with each receiving at least 1.
findings.observed: Board state reached: P1 turn 9 main phase, 17 energy; friendly Chakram Dancer (3 might) at base; three enemy units (Determined Sentry 1M, Sinister Poro 1M, Legion Rearguard 2M) at battlefield-player-2-bf-ogn-276-298. Attempting playSpell on Alpha Strike (player-1-main-999-unl-192-219) with those targets returns {error:"Move 'playSpell' condition not met", errorCode:"CONDITION_FAILED"} — the card is not enumerated as a legal move and direct execution is rejected.
